panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a human patient's lower limbs and feet demonstrating the congenital vertical talus rocker-bottom deformity, directly named in the caption and in-text. The convex plantar rocker-bottom contour is the classic clinical manifestation and is explicitly supported by the caption; the grayscale, poorly lit image precludes skin-tone assessment. Although the article's overall topic is a chromosome 2 interstitial deletion syndrome, the figure itself depicts congenital vertical talus, a configured target disease, so attribution is valid.

in_text_mentions: ht was 6.5 kg (<fifth percentile), height was 75 cm (<fifth percentile), and OFC was 36 cm (<fifth percentile). On physical examination, he could not hold his head steadily and barely reached for objects. He could coo, smile, and laugh, but could not wave. Further, he presented with frontal bossing with bitemporal narrowing, upslanted palpebral fissures (Figure 1), a small mouth with a high-arched palate, and posteriorly rotated ears (Figure 1). Congenital vertical talus with rocker bottom feet (Figure 2) as well as truncal and peripheral hypotonia along with hyperextensible joints were noted.
